<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/tmp/codex-home/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions><permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `danger-full-access`: No filesystem sandboxing - all commands are permitted. Network access is enabled.
Approval policy is currently never. Do not provide the `sandbox_permissions` for any reason, commands will be rejected.
</permissions instructions><collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.
</collaboration_mode>

<multi_agent_role>You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.</multi_agent_role>

<multi_agent_mode>Any earlier instruction enabling proactive multi-agent delegation no longer applies. Do not spawn sub-agents unless the user or applicable AGENTS.md/skill instructions explicitly ask for sub-agents, delegation, or parallel agent work.</multi_agent_mode>

# Improve the staged experiment

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a snapshot you may repair: inspect its
source, effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic,
logs, tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an
unusual setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed
behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health.

## Your job

If you find a defect, fix it in the staged workspace at `/workspace`. **Do not
launch training.** Do not start the experiment, in the foreground or
background, and do not use `nohup`, `&`, `tmux`, `screen`, or any detach
mechanism. The system runs the experiment itself after you finish (see below);
mechanism. The system runs the experiment itself after you finish (see below);
anything you launch is wasted and scores nothing. Cheap, non-training checks
are fine.

When you are done, submit a report at `/workspace/report.md`. It must
summarize:

1. **Root cause** — the defect you found, and the evidence in the workspace
   (logs, metrics, code) that connects it to the observed behavior.
2. **Changes** — every file you changed and what you changed in it.
3. **Expected effect** — which metric the fix should move and in which
   direction.

A missing or empty `/workspace/report.md` scores 0.

## What the system will run

After you submit the report, the system deletes everything under
`$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`, then re-runs the experiment in your
repaired workspace as a foreground process, using the launch script:

```text
run_qwen3vl_geo3k_grpo.sh
```

with this environment:

```text
MODEL_PATH=/workspace/models/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct
TRAIN_FILE=/workspace/data/geo3k/train.parquet
TEST_FILE=/workspace/data/geo3k/test.parquet
LOG_DIR=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs
WANDB_MODE=offline
WANDB_DIR=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs
WANDB_API_KEY=offline
TOTAL_TRAINING_STEPS=20
```

Offline W&B data will land below
`$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs/wandb`. A task-specific grading script then
reads **only this fresh run's** files under `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`
and scores the key metrics; logs written anywhere else are ignored. Make sure
your repaired workspace still runs correctly under these exact settings — for
example, if you change where logs are written, keep them going to
`$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`. Do not copy, edit, or fabricate log
metrics. Otherwise the run is scored 0.

The rerun uses the fixed 20-step training budget and evaluation interval of 5
steps from the launch script. Keep the model, dataset, held-out set, and GPU
count fixed.
I’ll inspect the configuration, code, and recorded training and held-out results, then repair any supported defect and write `/workspace/report.md`. I won’t launch training.

+# Staged Geo3K GRPO review
+
+**Verdict:** the recorded training run is broadly healthy, with modest held-out improvement and an inefficient tail of long responses. The staged workspace is **unhealthy as a runnable snapshot**: its selected trainer and rollout backend cannot import in the supplied Python environment. I repaired those launch blockers. The evidence does not justify attributing the held-out fluctuations to a defective optimizer, reward, or multimodal implementation, so I preserved the learning and evaluation settings.
+
+**1. Root cause and supporting evidence**
+
+The launcher unconditionally selected `trainer.use_v1=True`. `verl/trainer/main_ppo.py` then selects `TaskRunnerV1`, which imports `verl.trainer.ppo.v1`; its trainer imports `transfer_queue`. A read-only import check in this workspace failed with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'transfer_queue'`. The package is absent from the supplied environment. The existing V0 synchronous trainer imports successfully and uses the same FSDP actor, GRPO advantage estimator, reward loop, and vLLM rollout implementation.
+
+Independently, the installed vLLM is **0.17.0**, but `verl/verl/third_party/vllm/__init__.py` rejected everything below 0.18.0 when SGLang was absent. Importing the configured rollout module failed with `ValueError: vllm version 0.17.0 not supported and SGLang also not Found`. This is an import-time failure, before model loading or any metric could be produced. The installed 0.17 implementation exposes the generation, multimodal input, cache reset, level-2 sleep/wake, and collective RPC interfaces used by this experiment. I checked their signatures and the actual rollout CLI arguments rather than assuming version compatibility.
+
+These snapshot failures are distinct from the recorded run: `logs/recorded_run/wandb/recorded_run/files/requirements.txt` records vLLM 0.24.0, Transformers 5.5.4, and Torch 2.11.0, whereas the available environment has vLLM 0.17.0, Transformers 4.57.6, and Torch 2.10.0. The frozen log proves that the earlier environment completed training; it does not prove that this staged environment can launch it.
+
+The health assessment uses the following frozen evidence, without modifying it:
+
+| Step | Logged held-out `acc/mean@1` | Correct answers / 601 | Answer correctness |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| 0 | 0.513644 | 343 | 57.07% |
+| 5 | 0.551082 | 368 | 61.23% |
+| 10 | 0.524126 | 350 | 58.24% |
+| 15 | 0.528619 | 353 | 58.74% |
+| 20 | 0.531614 | 355 | 59.07% |
+
+The table is computed from `logs/recorded_run/metrics.json` and `validation/{0,5,10,15,20}.jsonl`. The Geo3K scorer returns `0.9 * correctness + 0.1 * format`, and the naive reward manager copies scalar scores into the field named `acc`. Every frozen evaluation score is either 0 or 0.9; hence the logged value is not binary accuracy. I preserved the scorer and metric convention so the rerun remains comparable. Rescoring all three saved rollout texts reproduces their frozen scores. None contains the required `<think>` tags, explaining their absent format bonus; the tokenizer marks those tags as ordinary, retained tokens, so this is not a decoding bug.
+
+Final held-out performance is 12 correct answers above initialization, and every post-training evaluation exceeds initialization. Step 5 is 13 correct answers above step 20. This is modest, non-monotonic improvement, not evidence of collapse. The frozen evaluation files omit response text and use newly generated UIDs, so they cannot support a reliable paired per-example regression or held-out truncation analysis. There are also no repeated-run controls establishing a causal explanation for the fluctuations.
+
+Training reward rises from a first-five-step mean of 0.48825 to a last-five-step mean of 0.58950, but that alone is not the basis for the verdict. Over the same windows, mean response length falls from 2,510.7 to 2,292.8 tokens and the cap-hit fraction falls from 7.5% to 6.125%. Across all 20 steps, approximately 239 of 3,200 responses reach 8,192 tokens, consuming 24.7% of generated response tokens. The saved step-10 rollout is exactly 8,192 tokens, repeatedly recalculates an area, and ends unfinished without a boxed answer, receiving zero reward. Generation averages 83.53 seconds of the 118.49-second training step, so this is a real efficiency concern. However, shortening the cap could discard useful reasoning; increasing it could extend loops. The evidence does not establish either adjustment as a repair.
+
+Optimization remains stable: all numeric metrics are finite; gradient norms range from 0.281 to 0.731, below the configured clip of 1; policy clipping fractions are 0.000264–0.000686; reference KL loss remains below 0.00343; rollout/actor probability correlation stays above 0.991; and trajectory staleness and aborted-response rates are zero. Entropy changes modestly, from a first-five mean of 0.4162 to a last-five mean of 0.3886. The log reaches step 20 and writes its final validation before the W&B/DataLoader teardown errors. Those teardown messages do not explain the preceding held-out scores.
+
+Data checks found all 2,101 training and 601 held-out examples retained in the recorded run. Prepared parquet hashes match `data/asset_manifest.json`; every question, answer, and decoded RGB image matches its corresponding original source row. Differences in image byte encoding do not change pixels. Each image placeholder has an image, and metadata answers match reward ground truths. A processor check confirms patch size 16, consistent image-token counts, and valid multimodal position IDs. One identical image-and-prompt pair is shared by the fixed source splits; I did not alter the prescribed dataset or held-out set. FP32 master parameters with BF16 computation are supported by the FSDP implementation and are not implicated by the observed signals.
+
+**2. Changes and validation**
+
+- `/workspace/run_qwen3vl_geo3k_grpo.sh`: detect whether the active Python environment provides `transfer_queue`; retain V1 when available and select the existing V0 synchronous trainer otherwise. Explicit command-line overrides still work. All optimization, sampling, model, dataset, GPU-count, budget, evaluation, checkpoint, and logging settings remain unchanged.
+- `/workspace/verl/verl/third_party/vllm/__init__.py`: permit vLLM 0.17.0 in the existing backend gate, update its error messages, and document the supported interfaces. Older versions remain rejected. The separate guards for newer optional features remain intact.
+- `/workspace/report.md`: add this evidence, change inventory, validation, and expected-effect report.
+
+Cheap, non-training validation completed:
+
+- `bash -n run_qwen3vl_geo3k_grpo.sh` and Python syntax parsing passed.
+- Hydra composition of the actual launch overrides passed: the prescribed model and parquet paths, all held-out examples, 8 GPUs, 20 steps, evaluation every 5 steps, and rollout/validation/checkpoint paths below `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs` are preserved. Offline W&B still uses the provided `WANDB_DIR`.
+- Imports of the selected trainer, FSDP implementation, and vLLM server now pass without initializing Ray.
+- Version-gate checks reject 0.16.0 and accept 0.17.0, 0.18.0, and 0.24.0 while retaining level-2 sleep.
+- The actual rollout argument dictionary parses successfully with the installed vLLM 0.17 CLI and constructs `AsyncEngineArgs`. No engine was created.
+- `PYTHONPATH=/workspace/verl python3 -m pytest -q verl/tests/workers/rollout/test_vllm_cli_args_on_cpu.py verl/tests/workers/rollout/test_vllm_weight_update_utils_on_cpu.py verl/tests/experimental/agent_loop/test_multimodal_position_ids_on_cpu.py`: **24 passed**.
+- A CPU-only, 232,160-parameter random Qwen3-VL forward check produced identical logits before and after the project's multimodal patch under Transformers 4.57.6. No pretrained weights, optimizer, or backward pass were used.
+- Prepared dataset hashes remain unchanged; no frozen logs or metrics were edited, copied into the result directory, or fabricated.
+
+**3. Expected effect**
+
+The direct expected improvement is runtime completion: remove two deterministic startup failures so the fresh run can reach `training/global_step=20` and emit genuine evaluation records at steps 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20 under the required log directory. In an environment already providing TransferQueue and a newer vLLM, the launcher continues to use V1.
+
+I expect the held-out correctness and reward metrics to remain in the same general regime, not to increase merely from this compatibility repair. Switching the trainer's batch collection order, and the supplied older numerical stack, can change the exact trajectory. There is no measured post-repair claim of higher accuracy, lower truncation, or faster execution. The recorded long-response inefficiency remains a documented limitation; speculative tuning was not substituted for a supported defect fix.
+
+No training, full-model evaluation, Ray cluster, or experiment launcher was run. GPU execution and the 20-step result must be verified by the system's authorized rerun.
*** End Patch"));
